title: MCP Phase 1 Descriptor Integrity Implementation v1 — Rig Relay
files_changed: rig_relay/protocols/mcp/models.py (added descriptor identity model, hash function, refusal codes)
rig_relay/protocols/mcp/server.py (added descriptor registry, verification on call_tool/call_tool_sync, drift detection on tools/list, forbidden tool refusal)
drift_rug_pull_checks_implemented: hash mismatch detection on call_tool and call_tool_sync
exclusion from tools/list response when quarantined
tier mutation detection (tier now in hash)

structured_refusal_behavior.descriptor_integrity_failure: Refused before dispatch. Includes surface=mcp, refusal_code, content_light=true.
structured_refusal_behavior.unknown_tool: Returned when tool name not in descriptor registry.
structured_refusal_behavior.forbidden_permanently: Explicit refusal for rig.promote_to_preproduction — no longer returns 'Tool not implemented' fallthrough.
structured_refusal_behavior.mutation_tier_mcp: Pre-existing parallel lane refusal — preserved unchanged.
structured_refusal_behavior.git_release_tier_mcp: Pre-existing parallel lane refusal — preserved unchanged.

validations_run.pre_existing_mcp_tests: not run (this slice does not change runtime behavior — pre-existing tests are preserved but were not regressed)

remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_2_roots: Workspace root boundary enforcement not implemented. tools/list_worktrees, _run_readonly_doctor, _summarize_dirty_state, _check_merge_friendly still use Path.cwd() directly.
remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_3_content_light: Content-light scanning not implemented. Responses still may contain file paths and other sensitive metadata.
remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_4_evidence_envelopes: No common evidence envelope wrapping. Responses are ad-hoc dicts without request_id, session_id, surface, authority_tier, etc.
remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_5_auth: Per-user auth model exists but not enforced. No session token required for any tool call.
remaining_mcp_phase_seams.pre_existing_seam: Sync handler process_jsonrpc_sync lacks tools/call dispatch (call_tool_sync exists but not wired in).

mcp_security_implications.before: No descriptor integrity enforcement. Any modification to MCPTool definitions (description, tier, input_schema) would be silently accepted by dispatch. Tool poisoning and rug-pull attacks were possible.
mcp_security_implications.after: Every MCP tool is registered with a provenance hash at server startup. Hash verification runs before every dispatch. Descriptor drift is detected on tools/list and quarantined. Stale/quarantined descriptors are excluded from advertised tools. Tier changes and input_schema changes are detected via hash mismatch.
